claims.statement: Termind separates Swift Testing by ownership: FrameworkTests protects portable shared-framework contracts, TFMTests covers macOS composition/native interaction/remote-session behavior, and TFITests covers mobile composition, scene behavior, and mobile presentation.

ArchitectureBoundaryTests checks module-specific import/construction and Persistence ownership boundaries, excludes concrete multiplexer dialect/service/runtime dependencies from neutral layers and Features, retains SSHPTYChannel StartupPreparation, and forbids direct concrete/vendor engine dependencies in SSHPTYChannel and ResumableTerminalClient; these source checks complement runtime tests.
MobileWorkspaceStore idempotently retires mobile.workspaces.v1 and mobile.recentlyClosed.v2 without decoding or migrating them, preserving unrelated settings for malformed and legacy-valid inputs.

Retired mobile snapshots are not a restoration channel; recently closed state remains app-instance local, grouped reopen is once-only and bounded, and external connections remain transient without replaying one-shot commands. Native close retains workspaces until discard; rejected/missing windows do not delete work. Activity URLs omit opaque references and reject extra parameters, and budget tests preserve whole focused entries.

Mobile app tests establish that conversations are shared across scenes while assistant navigation, selection, and drafts are scene-local, and that external connection workspaces are ephemeral rather than Vault or saved-workspace records.

SFTPTransferContext lets queued transfers retain an authenticated primary connection after the UI owner releases it, closes that connection only when no owner or transfers remain, and opens additional connections from a snapshot through a noninteractive request.

SFTP transfer-context fixtures exercise bounded per-host scheduling across contexts, donation/silent-interaction fallback, and cancellation/retired-generation refusal to fall back to the PTY, using controlled clients rather than live servers.

Security regression fixtures verify that agent authentication can use one-use credentials without mutating Vault state unless saving is requested, collect jump-host and destination authentication in route order, and coalesce concurrent authentication while preventing SFTP opening after cancellation.

SSH interaction-policy tests require forbidden requests, including Security Key authentication, to fail without showing host-key or keyboard-interactive UI; additional connection snapshots retain references instead of credential material, and clearing a configuration consumes secret values shared by copies.

Historical schemas migrate through the shared current V59 factory; migration endpoints omit V29/V32/V33 and retain frozen pre-color Snippet models. SnippetColorTests constructs V50 disk data, preserves content/relations/order, saves color and reopens.

Agent replay persistence tests verify frozen context/tool-result restoration, prevent replay-row duplication across later snapshots, remove replay backing on conversation deletion, and preserve a durable result recorded before the next snapshot.
MacOS tests that show windows or take focus must use the requiresVisibleWindow trait, which is enabled only by TERMIND_WINDOW_TESTS=1; normal test runs therefore skip them.

CloudKit safety fixture substitutes transport while retaining production coordinators, journals, record coding, batches and providers for all five categories; safety tests fence unsupported and malformed records without blocking compatible peers, retain fences across conflict/retry, check transactional rollback, and ensure fetched winners but not older or same-version losing records clear pending journal, engine queue and stale batches. Physical deletion and recreation causality are exercised separately.

CloudSyncSafetyPersistenceTests upgrades constructed V30/V39 stores through the current V59 factory across retired per-category quarantine tables and reopens interrupted categories with scoped blocks, recovery and pending intent intact; this is not live CloudKit proof.

Focused connection-history tests cover V31-to-V34 migration, independent device records and rename propagation, event lifecycle/tombstones, local-device filtering, newest-250 storage, 100-event desktop and 50-event mobile presentation and preferred-protocol quick actions while excluding Serial; these model tests do not prove multilingual native rendering.

The same-run SwiftData edit regression uses equal timestamps, reversed UUIDs, compacted production restoration, a legacy prefix invocation with inferred source ownership, backing-row counts, staging adoption and late-write attempts; it does not seed an unknown cutoff invocation. The empty-run regression separately proves live/restored ordering when the replacement clock precedes the retained run.

Failed/interrupted staging-adoption tests verify one real message/run/replay graph and restore provenance, state, failure and frozen context from a new ModelContext and repository over the same in-memory container rather than proving disk relaunch.

Composer regression covers compacted same-run display-prefix, tool, title, plan, compaction and run chronology retention; mobile exercises SwiftData restore and operations edit to compare live and restored prefix ownership.

Conversation operations reject a non-user replacement without invoking truncation and preserve visible messages and transcript when an injected repository truncation rejects; controller edit-failure and post-edit cancellation tests check captured replacement context, preserved history, and interrupted real-run adoption of staging. These port-level failures do not inject real SwiftData transaction faults.

Captured missing-model or missing-credential preparation failures construct a failed snapshot and keep preparation active until an asynchronous repository save succeeds; only then does the live conversation record failure, while a save error appends an assistant error instead. Controller tests gate the save and verify joining/projection ordering; missing-credential and navigation tests separately wait for a recorded failed save attempt, which does not itself prove save completion.

Manual compaction is refused while agent preparation is held at a memory snapshot barrier, without starting compaction activity; edit and cancellation fixtures also prohibit stale or cancelled prepared edits from entering truncation and join in-flight truncation before recording interruption.

After an edited replacement commits, a pending failed-run save blocks further edit and fork and later adopts the real failed-run ownership; if that save instead throws, preparation retires without adopting staging or recording a completed failed snapshot and displays an assistant error.

Tool presentation tests protect the composed AgentKit/Termind presenter ID namespace, presenter-ID-directed restored detail versus generic fallback for missing IDs, safe decoding of old metadata, and approval argument detail including the provided command rather than a blanket redaction guarantee.

MCP upload tests exercise scoped ticket capacity, acknowledged-offset resume and full digest, stream backpressure, cancellation and cleanup, conflict and terminal status with a fake SFTP client and controllable clock; a loopback HTTP test sends fresh and resumed bodies beyond the ordinary MCP body limit without a real remote SFTP server.

MobileBackgroundController retires a background lease once; platform-spy tests cover repeated/stale expiration, synchronous reentrant expiration during begin that preserves a replacement lease, and invalid task identifiers that expire without ending a UIKit task.

MobileCardTests protects offscreen tag limits, confirmation selection isolation, connection indicators, timestamps and draft-color persistence; it currently provides neither brand-contrast or measured-height checks nor an optional snippet screenshot export path.
Mobile key-window integration suites are opt-in and must run without parallel testing because UIKit presentation state is process-wide; macOS visible-window tests retain their own opt-in gate.

MobileAppTests now checks in-memory startup with the shared schema and empty repository rather than a bundled V28 migration/relaunch fixture. PersistenceCompatibilityTests constructs historical disk stores programmatically; V31/V34 retired-journal inputs and V35 native Device/account state are checked on repeated opens, while several other cases assert only the first migrated open.

The SwiftData repository ownership check uses a SwiftSyntax-based script to distinguish declarations from references and textual decoys; its regression tests cover both positive declarations and negative comments, strings and references.

Shared commerce tests cover the data-only ProPaywallState phase, ownership, expiration and access projection and use synthetic RevenueCat CustomerInfo with a fake purchase service to check entitlement validation, grace and refund boundaries, update ordering and coalesced refresh; neither tests remote dashboard rendering or live purchases.

Desktop and mobile Pro views host RevenueCatUI PaywallView with ProPaywallState-derived custom variables, loading/unavailable fallbacks, and purchase initiation permitted only without Pro access. Purchase/restore completion refreshes access, while purchase completion suppresses the next requested dismissal; the views do not forward start, cancellation or failure events to the controller.

HistorySyncTests covers native CloudKit fields, independent History/Device selection in the shared zone, terminal event tombstones, ignoring retired Vault-importer state, failed-initial-fetch recovery, missing Device projection repair without journal-version changes, structured safe logging and expected cancellation; SyncRecordEvolutionTests freezes literal Host V1 bytes and tests per-kind test-only Host V3 evolution while other kinds remain V1. These local fixtures do not prove deployed cloud delivery.

No current dedicated Pro paywall rendering fixture establishes RevenueCatUI dashboard layout; repository policy keeps offscreen layout/logic enabled while window/focus tests such as ChooserInteractionTests require explicit opt-in.

CloudSyncPhysicalDeletionTests drives production safety fixtures across record categories to ensure destructive zone deletions clear only the active replica and never resend its old snapshot, and checks that disk-persisted delete handoff, acknowledgement races and new incarnations remain distinct.

MobileSettingsPortTests use in-memory app composition and injectable secret/persistence/discovery seams to verify immediate SFTP preferences propagation without opening Settings, no cloud engines in test scene activation, provider draft/secret rollback on failures, non-resurrection after remote deletion and ignored late discovery after cancellation or deletion; these tests do not require a key window.

MobileConnectionPickerTests runs model and policy assertions without a key window and gates its multi-host picker navigation test on TERMIND_MOBILE_UI_TESTS, but its toolbar navigation tests also create a key window through withNavigation and currently lack an opt-in condition; serialization alone does not skip those cases by default.

Legacy mobile snapshot inputs are deleted and contribute no workspaces; the new descriptor store restores dormant lists without connecting. Cold-launch session tests now retain SSH, SFTP, Telnet, Mosh and Eternal Terminal records across old native-window discard before or after handoff, while existing native owners retain records until binding and explicit close.

Mobile reconciliation retains ownership while the native session exists and transfers missing sessions to an active destination only after saving the complete descriptor handoff. Save failure preserves source runtimes and owners. Live-source provenance permits late discard to close only transferred work from that source, whereas unbound cold-restored sources do not acquire that authority.

V41-to-V42 compatibility migrates an existing group with empty agent-message origin, conversation origin and delivery receipt sidecars; collaboration fixtures separately establish that persisting a delivered message confirms a queued receipt across SwiftData contexts without a stale downgrade, and that creation relations survive a disk reopen and stay scoped to requested chats.

Replay fixtures check that queued cancellation adopts edited staging without provider calls and restores authored text, images, attachments and frozen context from a fresh context; captured configuration failure adopts after failed snapshot save. Both join stopAndWait and check fullAccess and start/finish/message clock bounds. Synthetic V15 migration invents no historical context or replay rows.

Controller fixtures require archive and delete to await completion of a blocked preparation-failure save and retain the controller and conversation through the save after external references are released; they exercise in-process persistence ownership rather than crash durability.

Across Vault, History, Device, Settings and Metrics journals, safety persistence tests require repeated identical system-field writes and upload acknowledgements not to dirty SwiftData, while changing system fields or pending-upload state does produce changes.

Mobile workspace session fixtures direct assistant notifications to matching active or hidden owner scenes without stealing another scene's selection, and hold transfer clicks until an active scene is available, consuming them once; these exercise app/router ownership without a key-window dependency.

CloudSyncLifecycleTests uses an injected in-memory journal, fake transport and engine, failure hooks and continuation gates to prove fetch-before-send authorization, recovery fencing across failed or overlapping fetch/send operations, retired-engine callback rejection and fail-closed persistence/lookup failures; it does not operate a live CloudKit transport or a disk store.

CloudSyncLifecycleTests protects detached delegate task context for synchronization and cancellation, bounds combined saves and deletes at 250 while rejecting unjournaled deletes, and keeps invalid pending changes from consuming the request limit.

NotificationPreferencesTests coalesces initial authorization across scenes, avoids permission requests for disabled or bell-only settings and after failed preference loads, and checks remote notification Settings records do not echo, reject older versions and reset on tombstones; its V40 disk fixture upgrades to V41 and retains workspace preferences on reopen.

MobileMetricsJourneyTests is serialized and requiresKeyWindow-gated. Its injected sampler/key-window fixture retains a localized two-field challenge through navigation/width/type changes and submits once, restores the prior window and emits review images; default runs do not execute it without mobile UI opt-in.

macOS MetricsJourneyRenderingTests explicitly requires the visible-window opt-in; mobile MetricsJourneyTests uses the separate key-window opt-in for injected native presentation rather than real SSH delivery.
Persistence owns the V59 model set and migration factory, disables automatic CloudKit and rejects URL-plus-memory mode; platform entry points choose storage and own container lifetime.

On macOS the container factory acquires a per-store advisory file lease before SwiftData can open or migrate, reuses the same lock for canonicalized URL aliases within the process and retains it through the container lifetime; contention fails with inUse, whereas separate stores and in-memory containers do not contend.

A macOS lock fixture uses an independent process to prove that an occupied store cannot open, forced process exit releases the lease without deleting the stable lock file, and a subsequent open retains Vault host/key data; its sentinel case establishes that lock denial precedes database or WAL mutation.

The desktop startup guard checks running applications with the same bundle identifier before opening a real store, rejecting another process even when an older instance does not implement file locking; tests exercise the PID decision without showing an alert or launching another app.

Shared WebAuthn Vault metadata fixtures resolve destination and jump security-key references without Keychain, round-trip and apply external-key V2 records into an independent memory store, normalize legacy hardware storage and reject external software keys; failing persistence writes/deletes leave metadata unchanged, and V44 disk software keys survive V45 migration and repeated reopening.

MobileVaultFeatureTests uses in-memory app/editor fixtures for WebAuthn generation/import, invalid-reference rejection, software-key private material/passphrases, host/group mutations and forwarding without live transports or a key window; these tests do not prove native hardware-editor presentation.

ArchitectureBoundaryTests additionally prohibits direct StoreKit imports in Infrastructure commerce, isolates Firebase SDK imports to Infrastructure and requires collection-disabled diagnostic plist defaults; it checks targeted forwarding and mobile authentication ownership and requires additional-connection owners to reference snapshots instead of carrying full connection configurations.

Mobile workspace notification fixtures ensure newer assistant clicks supersede older clicks and stale window activation failures cannot reset newer requests, independently of UIKit window presentation.

Desktop TerminalContextMenuTests covers selection/blank-space/right-click-paste/live upload bindings. Ghostty gesture and dispatch internals require validation of the pinned upstream package, not inference from app tests; no local Ghostty maintenance submodule exists.

Always-on Find tests exercise action/focus ordering, idempotent dismissal, retained-query reopening and resize suspension; resume searches only the latest query, navigation is suppressed and closed search cannot reopen.

TerminalFindController retains query independently of presentation, restarts nonempty search when reopened and ignores already-closed dismissal. Mobile SSH, Mosh, Eternal Terminal and Telnet bind to it with native closure suppressing focus restoration; SFTP binds directly to its query and the workspace supplies execution/focus closures.

MobileToolbarSearchController owns one UISearchController, defers model synchronization out of SwiftUI updates, fences activation/edit/submit through native dismissal and resigns/publishes closed before deactivation so retained queries cannot be erased or presentation reopened mid-transition.

MobileTerminalSearchIntegrationTests is serialized and gated by TERMIND_MOBILE_UI_TESTS; its SSH regression repeats native, programmatic and terminal-focus-then-native cancellation three times and asserts active/responder/model state and retained query, including that an empty query leaves Find presented.

MobileTerminalSearchIntegrationTests verifies repeated SFTP filter cancellation/reopening retains the query and releases the responder, and clearing the filter leaves search active; SSH/SFTP journey visibility transitions preserve search-controller identity, while SSH also preserves the attached terminal view and retained-query reopening after journey dismissal.

Mobile search fixtures use local in-memory UIKit windows and simulated Journey/delegate dismissal; full-workspace SSH checks surface/output/generation retention across reopening. Cleanup restores/disconnects; neither fixture proves physical taps or a live remote transport.

Repository commands opt into mobile key-window validation with TEST_RUNNER_TERMIND_MOBILE_UI_TESTS=1, disabled parallel testing and narrow suite filters. Host traits read TERMIND_MOBILE_UI_TESTS; TFI includes TFITests/FrameworkTests without an explicit scheme environment entry for that flag.

MobileOperationConfirmationTests is serialized/mobile-UI gated and tests localized anchored versus centered popovers, action ordering and post-dismissal execution timing while restoring temporary key windows.

HostEditorBindingsTests exercises creation callbacks without changing existing selections, independent SSH/Telnet custom-versus-none identity choices, proxy default-port transitions and no recreation of removed proxies.
MobileWorkspacePresentationTests checks dismissal-before-import-result with once-only target consumption and preview-to-export sequencing using observable state machines without UIKit windows.

SSHPTYChannelLifecycleWireTests requires TERMIND_PTY_LIFECYCLE_FIXTURE and uses a local peer that never acknowledges exec CLOSE to check transport retirement on disconnect/owner release and SFTP sibling survival until final subsystem closure.

RetiredTerminalHighlightingTests verifies V46/V51 upgrade/reopen drops retired storage without losing other preferences, preparation removes inactive pending uploads, and malformed legacy conflicts/deletions do not quarantine or block active Settings records.

Remote-session continuation tests cover staging/save/connect ordering, proxy entered usernames, failed-save nonconnection and credential cleanup; controller tests cover teardown before retry, disconnect cancellation, host lookup precedence and stale progress rejection without real connections.

SessionPersistenceTests establishes nonblocking best-effort cleanup: explicit close queues only managed references, failed cleanup attempts once without retry, batches deduplicate identities and continue after failure, pre-start cancellation opens no connections, and timeout cancels cleanup. Passive termination, suspension, remote exit and detach enqueue no remote termination.

WorkspaceCloseConfirmationTests is an offscreen serialized suite proving populated windows need no live-connection confirmation while native delegate vetoes remain effective; theme edits flush when possible and unsaved drafts retain discard protection. Passive window close preserves managed recovery attachments, including closed-record reconstruction, and explicit close without a cleanup owner also preserves the reference.

Production macOS Quit returns terminateLater, saves terminal-theme edits and checks remaining unsaved themes, then rechecks pending SFTP edits before shutdown; open workspaces alone no longer cause a confirmation.

Mobile restoration tests distinguish passive discard from explicit close of a dormant managed workspace: passive discard preserves the remote reference for record-only reopening, explicit close queues cleanup and removes that reference, and neither replays an initial command. An ended live attachment must not be resurrected from its descriptor.

AgentReplayPersistenceTests simulates malformed historical structured result content and verifies recovery falls back to the frozen structured projection only for malformed envelopes, retaining plain output otherwise and preserving result identity, model projection and error state; this is a constructed recovery test rather than a process-crash test.

AgentReplayPersistenceTests verifies persisted request_user_secret output marks the handle expired and removes both the secret_handle field and its UUID, testing the persistence writer rather than a live secret service.

MCPServerMetadataTests constructs a V58 disk store, upgrades via the shared factory, retains server identity/tool policy, saves a description and checks reopening; rediscovery updates or clears descriptions without resetting access policy and legacy synced payloads tolerate its absence.

Assistant capture tests hold memory preparation while pane/context, permissions, skills and configuration change, verify the captured context and cancellation permission mode remain original, and reject revival by a credential added after capture.

WindowToolbarFindTests exercises desktop WindowModel routing without a native window: Vault pages select their Find target, Welcome uses content search, and terminal theme appearance queries remain independent across navigation.
